rubricDispositions.rationale: Focused tests cover the repaired durable workflow order, including server-side gather before model execution and a current-authority recheck before one route commit, plus the existing capability/domain, commit/review, and web queue suites. The exact-head pre-review lane report records focused classification, review-queue, codegen, contract, graph-boundary, layer-boundary, typecheck, and package test gates passing for head 27c0bdfd3fc0739c0788ab89186a676ef54230a8.

The web queue remains a feature/UI component, workflow contracts compose capabilities through the graph runner, the classification capability delegates to domain/classification helpers, and durable workflow validation stays outside React Flow. No provider, Slack, Nango, or direct database shortcuts were introduced into frontend or agent layers.

The repair is narrowly scoped to workflow gathering/current-authority seams and related docs/tests. It keeps reusable request loading in helper functions, records the workflow contract state in docs, and avoids broad rewrites or unrelated product changes. Existing compact/prettier-ignore generated-style contract formatting is accepted by the focused Prettier gate.

Durable schemas retain decision keys, generation fences, evidence/rationale hashes, effect keys, stage/status, lease, retry, messages, and allowed target metadata needed to inspect classification progress. The diff adds no logging of raw provider payloads, secrets, webhook bodies, or tokens.

The manifest sets a 300-line source slice budget. The exact-head lane report records status passed, four source slices, and slice sizes of 299, 251, 292, and 297 changed source lines, all within the per-slice budget and source slice limit.

The task plan explicitly leaves integration-owned regenerated Confect/Convex output outside the lane diff. The task changes manifest-owned generated docs/provenance and contract/source files only; no _generated Confect or Convex paths are edited, and the exact-head lane gate proves transient codegen passed.
